title: Encode a comment before it reaches the page

blocks.text: XSS happens when user text reaches a page as markup. The page's fix is **output encoding**: when a comment is rendered, replace `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` with `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`. It stores the original text and encodes at the point of rendering, so **every `&` is encoded**, even one the user typed as part of something that looks like an entity: the reader must see exactly what was typed.

items:
`render(comment)`: `"
" + encode(comment) + "
"`. The attribute is single-quoted, so **a single quote must be encoded too**.

cases.says: A script tag with double quotes, "Tom & Jerry" and a bold tag come out HTML-encoded, the last one inside the comment div.
A single quote is encoded as ', so it cannot end the single-quoted class attribute.
Text the user typed as "<", "<" or "&" is encoded again, so the reader sees exactly what was typed.
encode(null) is "" and render(null) is an empty comment div, not the text null.

origin.section: 2. Rendering user input directly in HTML

concepts: XSS is prevented by encoding output for the context it is rendered in: &, <, >, " and ' become HTML entities at the point of rendering.
